title: The Snake and the File

full_text:
A venomous serpent slithered into a blacksmith's workshop in search of mice. Slithering across the workbench, his cold skin struck a heavy, hardened steel file used by the smith to sharpen iron tools.

Believing the file had struck him, the spiteful snake coiled in fury and sank his sharp fangs deep into the steel. He gnawed with venomous malice, determined to crush the stubborn object.

Presently, the serpent felt his mouth filling with warm liquid. Believing he had drawn blood from his foe, he bit harder and harder, until his fangs snapped, his gums were shredded to ribbons, and his jaws were ground away upon the hardened steel.

The lifeless file remained cold and intact, while the dying snake perished of his own blind malice, learning too late that futile rage against superior strength ruins only the aggressor.
moral: Never vent your malice against that which cannot be harmed, lest you destroy yourself.
